theme_strategy.style_fusion: Mission Control Technical HUD (blueprint grid, isometric telemetry, glowing reticles, high-contrast amber/cyan/emerald status gauges) blended with Clean Futuristic SpaceX aesthetics (ultra-crisp borders, minimalist white/graphite typography, segmented cards, pill badges).
theme_strategy.emotional_tone: Astronaut Command Simulation: precise, authoritative, immersive, cinematic, high-stakes decision making with real NASA telemetry aesthetics.
theme_strategy.viewport_priority: Desktop-first command center with multi-panel HUD and responsive mobile adaptations (stacking modules into tabs/sheets).

rules.labels_and_callouts: font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.18em] text-cyan-400/90 font-semibold
rules.body_text: font-sans text-sm sm:text-base leading-relaxed tracking-normal text-slate-200

entry_surfaces./: Branded Mission Control Entry — split screen: left Astronaut Enrollment terminal (callsign, PIN, specialization, agency ID), right live telemetry stream with NASA rocket schematics and flight readiness status.
entry_surfaces./builder: Proteus-like Rocket Assembly Workspace — left NASA part inventory library, center blueprint canvas with live stage stacking & drag reorder, right telemetry & compatibility diagnostics panel.
entry_surfaces./simulation: Orbital Flight & Planetary Launch Simulation — top flight HUD telemetry (TWR, velocity, altitude, delta-v), center trajectory starfield viewport with timed obstacle crisis overlays, right decision log & planet destination tracker.
entry_surfaces./hangar: NASA Historic Fleet Hangar & Upgrade Depot — filterable gallery of legendary NASA rockets (Saturn V, Space Shuttle, SLS, Atlas V, Delta IV Heavy) with NASA specs, point unlock triggers, and upgrade workshop.
entry_surfaces./profile: Astronaut Flight Dossier & Mission Log — flight history, explored celestial bodies, badge credentials, total flight points, and simulation performance charts.

layout_and_grids.shell_layout: Top HUD Bar (Agency status, MET timer, active astronaut callsign, point balance, sound toggle) + Main Content Viewport + Bottom Diagnostic Status Strip.

visual_enhancers.blueprint_grid: background-image: radial-gradient(rgba(0, 229, 255, 0.15) 1px, transparent 0), linear-gradient(to right, rgba(0, 229, 255, 0.05) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(0, 229, 255, 0.05) 1px, transparent 1px); background-size: 24px 24px, 24px 24px, 24px 24px;

component_hierarchy.name: NavigationHUD
component_hierarchy.description: Top telemetry bar showing NASA insignia, active astronaut ID, points score, explored planets counter, sound toggle, and tab switches: [Builder, Launch Sim, Fleet Hangar, Upgrades, Dossier].

component_hierarchy.name: AstronautAuthModal
component_hierarchy.description: Astronaut credentials enrollment with Callsign, Agency ID (NASA/JSC-XXXX), Specialization (Flight Commander, Propulsion Specialist, Orbital Navigator, Systems Engineer), and Security PIN.

component_hierarchy.name: RocketBuilderCanvas
component_hierarchy.description: Proteus-style interactive blueprint builder with snap-to-stack slots: Payload Capsule -> Upper Stage -> Interstage -> Lower Fuselage/Fuel Tanks -> Rocket Engines -> Boosters/Fins. Drag-and-drop or click-to-attach, live reordering, and live mass/TWR/Delta-V calculation.

component_hierarchy.name: PartsLibraryDrawer
component_hierarchy.description: Categorized NASA historical & modern part catalog: Command Pods (Apollo CSM, Orion, Dragon), Fuel Stages (S-IC, S-II, S-IVB, SLS Core), Engines (F-1, J-2, RS-25, Merlin 1D, Raptor), Boosters (SRBs, Shuttle Boosters), Aerodynamics (Titan Titanium Fins, Grid Fins).

component_hierarchy.name: CompatibilityGuidePanel
component_hierarchy.description: NASA Flight Surgeon & Engineering Guide: detects incompatible part pairings (e.g. TWR < 1.1 = rocket won't lift, payload too heavy, engine mount diameter mismatch) and gives 1-click 'Select Alternative Part' recommendations.

component_hierarchy.name: MissionFlightSimulator
component_hierarchy.description: Dynamic launch and transit simulation to Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, or Europa. Features stage staging animations, atmospheric exit, orbital insertion, live countdown obstacles with critical decision choices, and % outcome calculator (100% Success, Partial Success, Mission Abort).

component_hierarchy.name: ObstacleCrisisCard
component_hierarchy.description: Time-sensitive incident card (e.g., 'Excessive Fuel Consumption detected during burn', 'Solar Flare Radiation Spike', 'Micrometeoroid Hull Puncture') presenting 2-3 engineering countermeasures with countdown timer.

component_hierarchy.name: FleetHangarGallery
component_hierarchy.description: Curated museum and active flight pad for real NASA rockets (Saturn V, Space Shuttle, SLS Artemis, Atlas V, Titan IV, Delta IV Heavy, Falcon 9/Heavy) with full specs and instant 'Fly This Rocket' launch trigger.

component_hierarchy.name: UpgradesWorkshop
component_hierarchy.description: Spend flight exploration points on upgrades: Engine Specific Impulse (+Isp), Aerodynamic Heat Shielding, Deep-Space Navigation AI, Cryogenic Fuel Insulation.

component_hierarchy.name: PlanetSelectorModal
component_hierarchy.description: Interactive celestial body catalog with NASA planetary data (gravity, distance, atmosphere, required delta-v, hazards) and curated real NASA imagery.

shuttle_launch_hero.description: Space Shuttle Challenger launching from Kennedy Space Center with plume and tower

mars_planet_view.description: High-resolution real view of Mars on black starry background

saturn_v_hangar.description: Rocket engines and multi-stage booster inside NASA Vehicle Assembly Building

space_rocket_liftoff.description: Orbital rocket ascending during daytime with massive thrust column

deep_space_mars_atmosphere.description: Atmospheric rim glow of Martian horizon in deep space

rocket_thrust_tail.description: Detailed vertical rocket stage structure with external piping and booster clamps

motion_and_microinteractions.hud_telemetry_tickers: Smooth counting animation using motion/react or setInterval for Delta-V, altitude, speed, and point gains.
motion_and_microinteractions.stage_assembly_snap: Spring physics on dropped or clicked rocket stages snapping into vertical alignment with sound trigger/visual pulse.
motion_and_microinteractions.launch_shake_effect: CSS keyframe shake on the launch viewport during T-0 to T+10s liftoff burn.
motion_and_microinteractions.crisis_countdown_bar: Urgent pulsing amber/red progress bar indicating remaining seconds (e.g. 10s) before emergency choice resolves.
motion_and_microinteractions.hover_state_rule: Every interactive HUD card lifts with `hover:-translate-y-0.5 hover:border-cyan-400 hover:shadow-[0_0_15px_rgba(0,229,255,0.2)] transition-all duration-200`.

accessibility_and_testing.wcag_aa_contrast: All text and telemetry values meet minimum 4.5:1 contrast against dark background. Use bright cyan (#38BDF8), white (#F8FAFC), amber (#FBBF24), or emerald (#34D399).
accessibility_and_testing.reduced_motion: Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by disabling launch screen shake and rapid starfield animations.
accessibility_and_testing.test_attributes: All buttons, tabs, drag items, inputs, crisis option buttons, and launch triggers MUST have `data-testid` attributes (e.g., `data-testid="astronaut-login-submit"`, `data-testid="launch-mission-btn"`, `data-testid="crisis-choice-0"`, `data-testid="part-item-f1-engine"`, `data-testid="hangar-fly-saturn-v"`).

instructions_to_main_agent: 1. Build the complete NASA Rocket Command & Simulation platform with both Page 1 (Custom Rocket Builder + Launch Simulation with Obstacle Crisis Decisions) and Page 2 (NASA Historic Fleet Hangar + Points System + Upgrades Shop + Astronaut Profile).

2. Seed rich, authentic NASA data for parts (Apollo, Shuttle, Artemis SLS, Titan, Saturn V, Atlas V), realistic mass/thrust/Isp equations for Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR) and Delta-V (Tsiolkovsky rocket equation calculation).
3. Implement the Beginner Help Guide module that detects incompatible setups (e.g., insufficient thrust, missing payload, unbalanced stages) with 1-click alternative part replacement.
4. Create multiple destination worlds (Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Europa, Titan, Saturn) with real NASA distances, gravity, and atmospheres.

5. Implement at least 6 unique obstacle scenarios with 2-3 engineering choices each (e.g., fuel leak, solar radiation flare, guidance gyro drift, staging separation jam, thermal tile loss, atmospheric drag peak).
6. Award points in the 3 specified ways: Mission Completion, Overcoming Obstacles, Exploring Planets. Points immediately unlock upgrades in the Upgrades Shop.
7. Include sound effects toggle (synthesized Web Audio API retro telemetry beeps, launch rumble, alert klaxons) for maximum immersion.
8. Keep all data persistent in localStorage + backend database so astronauts keep their earned points, unlocked upgrades, and custom rocket blueprints across refreshes.
